title: Clear and Resize the Arrangement Loop Region
text:
The loop-region editing in Nota’s arrangement timeline already feels easy and flexible. However, I haven’t found a clear way to remove the loop region, and I can’t seem to adjust its start and end boundaries independently.

This refers to the highlighted loop range in the timeline ruler above the tracks, not to the contents or boundaries of an individual clip.

Clear the Loop Region
Provide a discoverable Clear Loop Region command, for example in the region’s context menu.
,
Distinguish clearing the range from temporarily disabling loop playback.
,
Clearing the region must not delete or modify clips, notes, automation, or other project content.
,

Adjust Both Boundaries
Allow dragging the start and end edges independently to shorten or extend the range.
,
Preserve the opposite boundary when resizing one edge.
,
Respect the current snapping setting, with an accessible way to make finer adjustments.
,
Keep moving the entire range distinct from resizing its boundaries.
,

Make Resizing Discoverable
Show a horizontal resize cursor when hovering over either draggable boundary.
,
Subtly highlight the active edge and provide a sufficiently generous hit area.
,
Show the resulting start, end, or length while dragging.
,

Support Undo/Redo for clearing, moving, and resizing the loop region.

If these interactions already exist, make them easier to discover. The goal is to preserve the current simplicity while making removal and boundary adjustments clear and predictable.

title: Smooth Transitions Between Themes
text:
Switching between Nota’s themes currently changes the appearance abruptly, particularly when moving between a light and a dark theme.

Add a short, smooth transition to make these changes feel less harsh while keeping theme selection responsive.

Suggested behavior
Use a subtle fade or color transition of approximately 200 ms as a starting point, with a gentle ease-in-out curve.
,
Transition backgrounds, panels, borders, text, and icons together so the interface remains visually coherent.
,
Maintain readable contrast throughout the transition and avoid a bright flash between dark themes.
,
Keep controls responsive; the transition must not block interaction or interrupt audio processing.
,
If another theme is selected mid-transition, move smoothly toward the latest selection rather than queuing multiple animations.
,

Accessibility and Performance
Respect the operating system’s reduced-motion preference, using an immediate change or an appropriately reduced transition.
,
Avoid unnecessary rendering work when the transition is complete.
,
Do not animate the initial theme application at startup in a way that briefly exposes the wrong theme.
,

A duration around 150–250 ms would be worth testing; 200 ms seems like a reasonable default. The goal is a quick, understated transition rather than a slow or decorative animation.

title: Open the Changelog from the Status-Bar Version Number
text:
Make the version number displayed at the bottom-right of Nota’s main window, next to the sample rate, clickable.

Expected behavior
Clicking the version number opens Nota’s existing What’s New/changelog view inside the app, rather than introducing a separate duplicate view.
,
Initially show the release notes for the currently installed version, clearly labeled with its version number and release date.
,
Allow browsing other available changelog entries, ideally with search.
,
Provide an optional View on GitHub link to the corresponding release, where available.
,
If an in-app changelog is not available, opening the matching official release page is a useful fallback.
,

Interaction details
Add a subtle hover state and a tooltip such as View release notes so the interaction is discoverable.
,
Make the version control keyboard-focusable and activatable with Enter or Space.
,
Allow the in-app view to close with Escape and restore focus appropriately.
,
Keep release notes for the installed version available offline where practical.
,

Clicking the version number should show what changed in that version, without starting an update or interrupting the current project.

title: Visible Default Values and Per-Setting Reset
text:
Settings can be changed accidentally while clicking or navigating with the keyboard, sometimes without the user noticing. Every setting with a defined default should make that default discoverable and provide a straightforward way to restore it.

Show the Default
Display the default value and its unit, for example: Default: X semitones.
,
Keep this information easy to find without cluttering the interface, such as in a setting’s description or details popover.
,
Subtly indicate when the current value differs from its default.
,
Make default information accessible with the keyboard as well as the pointer.
,

Reset Individual Settings
Provide Reset to Default for each applicable setting.
,
Make the command accessible without requiring a mouse-only gesture.
,
Clearly identify which setting will be reset.
,
Allow the reset itself to be undone where technically possible.
,
For device-dependent settings, explain what the default means; never substitute an arbitrary value when no universal default exists.
,

Recover Previous Values
Resetting to the default and undoing an accidental change solve different problems. A user’s previous value may have been intentionally customized.

Support Undo/Redo for settings changes wherever technically possible, including changes made through keyboard input. Clearly explain any exceptions or changes with external side effects.

Optional Section Reset
A separate Reset This Section command could restore a whole category. Show its scope and request confirmation before resetting multiple settings, particularly audio or MIDI configuration.

Prevent Accidental Edits
Keep keyboard focus clearly visible and distinguish navigation from value editing. Navigating categories must not modify a parameter in another area.

The goal is to make defaults understandable and recovery predictable, without forcing users to remember every previous value or reset unrelated settings.

title: Automatic Keyboard Focus for Search Fields and Filters
Advanced Multi-Device Controller Support – Independent Gamepads & Keyboards
Keyboard Navigation for the Settings Sidebar
text:
Make all Settings categories accessible directly from the keyboard, including Audio, MIDI, Gamepads, Remote, Plug-ins, Downloads, Library, Appearance, and Shortcuts.

Expected behavior
Use Tab/Shift+Tab to move focus between the sidebar and the settings controls.
,
When the sidebar has focus, use ↑/↓ to move between categories.
,
Skip non-interactive group headings such as Devices, Plug-ins, and General.
,
Keep the focused category clearly visible and automatically scroll it into view when necessary.
,
Allow the selected page to open directly during navigation, or use Enter/Space to activate it, following a consistent interaction model.
,
Keep focus in the sidebar when switching pages so users can continue navigating without repeatedly refocusing it.
,
Make all interactive controls within each page keyboard-accessible as well.
,

Prevent accidental changes
Sidebar navigation must never alter a setting on the right. For example, pressing ↑/↓ to switch categories must not accidentally change the MIDI bend range.

Keys should act only on the currently focused control, with a clear visual distinction between navigating categories and editing values. Open dropdowns should handle their own navigation, and Escape should close the dropdown before closing Settings.

Goal
Open Settings → navigate categories → reach and edit the intended control → return to category navigation, without using the mouse.

Command Palette access can complement this, but the visible Settings interface should remain directly keyboard-operable.

title: Automatic Frequency-Based EQ Band Renumbering
text:
I would love an optional feature that automatically renumbers EQ bands according to their frequency positions, from lowest to highest.

Currently, in complex EQ workflows, adding a new band between existing bands can result in confusing numbering that no longer reflects the frequency spectrum.

Requested functionality:

Automatically number EQ bands from low to high frequencies.
,
Dynamically update the displayed numbering whenever bands are inserted, removed, or moved.
,
Optionally allow users to retain manual or original numbering.
,
Preserve stable internal parameter identities independently of visual band numbers.
,
Keep automation curves, automation lanes, parameter assignments, MIDI mappings, controller assignments, and other relevant references connected to the correct EQ bands.
,
Never accidentally reassign automation or control mappings to a different band.
,
Maintain consistent numbering throughout the entire application, including EQ views, parameter menus, automation editors, and related controls.
,
Handle overlapping bands, frequency crossings, presets, project reloads, and undo/redo safely.
,

Implementation suggestion: Treat the displayed band number as a dynamic visual identifier rather than the actual internal parameter identity. Every band should retain a stable unique ID.

This would make EQ workflows much more intuitive while maintaining full compatibility with existing projects and automation.

title: Always-Visible Custom EQ Band Labels with Expandable Notes
text:
I would love to have a labeling and note-taking system directly integrated into Nota's EQ interface.

Every EQ band should have an optional custom label that is immediately visible above or below its corresponding node in the frequency graph, without requiring the user to open an inspector or additional menu.

Clicking or tapping that label should expand a larger text field where users can add detailed notes explaining the purpose of the band.

Suggested features:

Custom short labels for individual EQ bands.
,
Labels always visible in the main EQ graph when enabled.
,
Expandable multiline notes accessible directly from each label.
,
Automatic saving of labels and notes with the project or preset.
,
Labels and notes permanently associated with their specific EQ bands, even when bands are moved or renumbered.
,
Smart positioning to prevent label collisions when multiple bands are close together.
,
Optional global show/hide toggle for labels.
,
Easy editing with mouse, keyboard, trackpad, and touchscreen where supported.
,
No impact on DSP performance, audio latency, or automation.
,

Example:
Label: 'Resonance Control'
Expanded note: 'This band reduces a narrow resonance that becomes especially noticeable during sustained notes. Avoid excessive attenuation to preserve the natural sound.'

This would make complex EQ setups easier to understand at a glance and would be particularly valuable when returning to older projects or collaborating with other users.

title: Dismissible Start Screen and Settings with Theme-Aware Background Blur
text:
Dismissal
The start screen currently cannot be dismissed with Escape or by clicking outside it. Support both interactions, with consistent behavior for Settings where applicable:

Press Escape to close the panel.
,
Click outside the panel to dismiss it.
,
Keep an explicit close button available.
,
Restore keyboard focus to the previous control or workspace after closing.
,
An outside click should dismiss the panel without also activating controls underneath.
,
If a nested menu or popup is open, Escape should close that first.
,
Never silently discard unapplied settings. Preserve them or ask before discarding changes.
,

Theme-Aware Backdrop
Apply a subtle blur to the interface behind the start screen and Settings, combined with a translucent overlay that matches the active theme:

Dark theme: a dark neutral overlay.
,
Light theme: a light neutral overlay, rather than applying the same dark tint.
,

Keep the panel itself sharp and readable. The backdrop should provide visual separation without making the surrounding workspace disappear. This is a visual preference intended to give these panels a calmer, more polished appearance.

Transitions and Accessibility
Fade the backdrop in and out smoothly without delaying interaction.
,
Respect reduced-motion and reduced-transparency preferences where available.
,
Offer a simple non-blurred fallback with sufficient contrast.
,
Keep rendering lightweight and avoid affecting audio performance.
,

title: More Intuitive Settings Window Dismissal
text:
Currently, when opening Settings via Cmd+, on macOS, I've noticed that the window cannot be dismissed using Escape or by clicking outside the Settings panel.

Personally, I would expect both interactions to work, as they are common and intuitive ways to dismiss dialogs and similar interface elements.

Suggested Improvements


Close Settings with Escape
,

• Pressing Escape should close the Settings window.
• This should work regardless of which settings category or control currently has keyboard focus.
• If a dropdown, popup, or another temporary interface element is open, Escape should dismiss that element first, following standard UI conventions.
• Any pending changes should be handled safely and consistently with Nota's existing settings behavior.


Close Settings by Clicking Outside
,

• Clicking outside the Settings panel should dismiss it.
• This would be particularly intuitive if Settings is implemented as a modal overlay.
• If there are unsaved changes requiring confirmation, clicking outside should not silently discard them.
• If Settings is implemented as a separate native window rather than a modal overlay, the behavior should follow the respective operating system's conventions.


Cross-Platform Consistency
,

Ideally, these interactions should behave consistently across macOS, Windows, and Linux, while respecting platform-specific UI conventions.

Expected Behavior
• Open Settings using the existing keyboard shortcut.
• Press Escape to dismiss Settings.
• Alternatively, click outside the Settings panel to dismiss it, where appropriate.
• Return to the previous workspace without unnecessary additional interactions.

Overall Goal

Make opening and closing Settings feel more intuitive, predictable, and consistent with established desktop application conventions.

This is primarily a UX improvement suggestion rather than necessarily a bug report.
